blocks.prompt: 6. Find the general solution of the differential equation \(\frac{dy}{dx} = 2x\sqrt{1 - y^2}\).
blocks.explanation:
Right side \(2x\sqrt{1 - y^2}\) hai: \(2x\) sirf \(x\) ka function aur \(\sqrt{1 - y^2}\) sirf \(y\) ka.
Yeh zarb \(g(x)h(y)\) hai, is liye equation separable hai.
Find kya karna hai? General solution, aur behtar hai ke \(y\) ko akela likhein.
Plan: alag karenge, \(\int\frac{dy}{\sqrt{1 - y^2}} = \sin^{-1}y\) lagayenge, phir \(\sin\) le kar \(y\) nikalenge.
steps:
Diya gaya: \(\frac{dy}{dx} = 2x\sqrt{1 - y^2}\), \(|y| < 1\).
Maloom karna: general solution.
Tareeqa: Equation separable hai. \(\sqrt{1 - y^2}\) ko \(dy\) ke neeche aur \(2x\) ko \(dx\) ke saath rakh kar integrate karenge.

Variables alag karein
\[\dfrac{dy}{\sqrt{1 - y^2}} = 2x\,dx\]
Kyun: Dono taraf \(\sqrt{1 - y^2}\) se divide kiya aur \(dx\) se multiply kiya. Ab har variable apni jagah par hai.

Dono taraf integrate karein
\[\int\dfrac{dy}{\sqrt{1 - y^2}} = \int 2x\,dx\]
\[\sin^{-1}y = x^2 + C\]
Kyun: Left par standard integral \(\sin^{-1}y\) (Question 2 jaisa). Right par power rule: \(\int 2x\,dx = 2 \cdot \frac{x^2}{2} = x^2\).

\(y\) ko akela karein
\[y = \sin(x^2 + C)\]
Kyun: \(\sin^{-1}\) ka ulta kaam \(\sin\) karta hai. Dono taraf \(\sin\) liya to \(\sin(\sin^{-1}y) = y\) bacha. Kitab ka jawab isi shakal mein hai.
Dhyan dein: \(y = \sin x^2 + C\) likhna ghalat hai; constant \(\sin\) ke andar hai, bahar nahi.

Tasdeeq
\[\dfrac{dy}{dx} = 2x\cos(x^2 + C)\]
\(\sin^{-1}y = x^2 + C\) hamesha \(\left[-\frac{\pi}{2}, \frac{\pi}{2}\right]\) mein hota hai, jahan \(\cos\) negative nahi hota, is liye
\[\cos(x^2 + C) = \sqrt{1 - y^2}\]
Kyun: \(\cos^2 + \sin^2 = 1\) se \(\cos = \sqrt{1 - \sin^2} = \sqrt{1 - y^2}\). To \(\frac{dy}{dx} = 2x\sqrt{1 - y^2}\), di hui equation mil gayi.
